claims.text: Helm is a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
Helm is open source under Apache License 2.0 and the Helm project does not ship a commercial tier.
In Pulumi, resource ordering is derived from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready and independent resources deploy in parallel.
Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind, defined in pkg/release/v1/util/kind_sorter.go in the Helm source.
Helm chart authors can't declare dependencies between resources or subcharts except through hook weights.

The Helm docs state that "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's kind order begins with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with unlisted kinds including custom resources last.
Helm uninstall runs the kind order list in reverse.
Helm sends sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and doesn't wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm subchart objects are merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind, so chart dependencies don't control install order.
Helm chart hooks are ordered with helm.sh/hook-weight annotations, and hook resources are not managed by Helm as part of the release.
Native sequencing for resources and subcharts has been proposed in HIP-0025, which is still a draft.
Pulumi Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to become ready before creating dependents, deploys independent resources in parallel, and deletes follow the graph in reverse.
helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for outside dependencies.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Pulumi and Helm together.
Pulumi orders the chart install after the resources its values depend on.
There are three common ways to adopt Pulumi alongside or in place of Helm; using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program is the most common adoption pattern.
helm.v4.Chart registers each chart object as a Pulumi resource so children show in plan output, drift detection, and state.
Helm merges objects from a chart and its dependencies into a single set, sorts by kind, and applies in that order, so declaring a subchart dependency doesn't make it install first.
Helm favors fast revision-based rollback of a single release; Pulumi favors scriptable control over resources from many providers.
